key_insight: Architectural differences in attention (uniform vs. trainable) do not produce fundamentally different algorithms for modular addition: both produce topologically and geometrically equivalent representation manifolds, implementing the same underlying computation.
problem_solved: Resolving a debate from the Clock vs. Pizza interpretations about whether different attention designs necessarily yield distinct circuits and representations for modular addition.
method: Compare the Clock and Pizza interpretation frameworks across architectures with uniform and learnable attention to identify representational correspondences.
Analyze the geometry and topology of learned activation manifolds (e.g., manifold shape, continuity, and mapping) to test equivalence claims.
Use alignment and invariance tests (empirical manifold comparisons and circuit-level mapping) to demonstrate the same algorithmic implementation.
impact: Shows that interpretability conclusions about algorithmic differences should account for geometric/topological equivalence, simplifying how practitioners reason about architecture choices and transfer of learned circuits across attention variants.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic of Clock vs. Pizza circuits with arrows showing a mapping that collapses them into the same manifold.
3D manifold renderings (colored by input/output phases) for both architectures demonstrating geometric overlap/alignment.
Topology diagram (e.g., homeomorphism illustration) showing continuous deformation from one representation to the other.
Flowchart summarizing the analysis pipeline: model variants → representation extraction → geometry/topology comparison → equivalence decision.
paper_title: On the geometry and topology of representations: the manifolds of modular addition
paper_authors: Gabriela Moisescu-Pareja, Gavin McCracken, Harley Wiltzer, Vincent Létourneau, Colin Daniels
